title: Phrases
goal: Two common words share one stroke when their keys do not collide: two strokes become one.

blocks.x: *of* is [[of|-F]], *the* is [[the|-T]]. They share no key, so pressing both, [[of the|-FT]], is a stroke nothing else uses: *of the*, the commonest word pair in the language, in one stroke instead of two.
A phrase is the **union of the keys** of the two words' strokes. It can be derived from the two words; if the keys collide, no phrase exists.
Striking the two words in sequence still works; the phrase stroke is an optional shortcut, adoptable one phrase at a time.
Some phrases are the first stroke of a longer word with a word fused in: *the utility* is [[the utility|AOUT/+EULT]]. Learn the two-word ones first.
